To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supplementation of yeast culture and enzymes can improve fermentation characteristics and in vitro degradability of cereal straw.
supplementation of fibrolytics and yeast culture can improve the in vitro fermentation of cereal straw, and that the effect is additive.
the application of yeast culture and/or fibrolytic enzymatic preparation could improve in vitro fermentation characteristics and IVDMD/IVOMD of cereal straws.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of yeast culture on the fermentation characteristics of cereal straws and the effects of the interaction between yeast culture and fibolytic enzymes on in vitro fermentation of cereal strawns.
the effects of yeast culture (Saccharomyces cerevisiae, YC) and fibrolyic enzyme preparation (contaning cellulase and xylane, FE) on in vitro rumen fermentation characteristics of cereal straws (CS).
the effects of yeast culture on the in vitro gas production of cereal straws and the interaction between fibrolytics and yeast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
yeast culture and fibrotic enzymes can be used as feed supplements to improve the nutritive value of cereal straws and their utilization in the ruminant digestive tract.
the supplementation of yeast culture and/or fibrolytic enzymatic preparations can improve the in vitro fermentation characteristics, IVDMD and OM disappearance of cereal straws.
the application of yeast culture and/or fibrolytic enzymatic preparation can improve the in vitro gas production characteristics of cereal straws.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of yeast culture and enzymes could be a potential strategy for improving the nutritive value of cereal straws and their utilization in ruminants.
supplementation of fibrolyctic enzyme and yeast could improve the in vitro digestibility of cereal straws.
yeast culture and fibolytic enzyme supplementation could be used to enhance the in vitro gas production of cereal straws.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of fibrolytics and yeast can enhance in vitro gas production of cereal straws.
the application of yeast and fibrolytics could improve the fermentation characteristics of cereal straws in vitro.
the use of a yeast culture combined with a fibrolytic enzymatic preparation can be used to improve the fermentation characteristics of low quality forage.
